title: It Fits in a Post
format: a demonstration of something a member made, credited

taken.from 1:17: The slabs marked with her own sign dropping onto a pile beside the desk; Eppy calling each one; the pile passing the desk and Larry and leaving the top of the frame; the camera craning after it and giving up; the button from behind the pile; a glance label that keeps this proof apart from the news.
taken.from 2:17: Her post small and complete at the left edge all the way through; her puppet saying the proof while the studio builds it, the notation respelled and never reworded; each bracket twice as wide as the last, out through the wall; her square landing on her own card and nowhere else.

jokes: The call and the reply: her puppet says 'now is your time to shine, you got this' into a follow spot, and Sibyl reads what came back, whole. Both posts are real and in order. The reply ends on zetaof1's own joke about the handle, and the next thing said is her post that fits. The studio makes no remark on it; the pile is the remark.
The count: the brackets double, eight terms, sixteen, thirty-two, through the wall, and Eppy's call is the same every time. It is her last word.
Sibyl's ruling, 'At least.', said as the pile leaves the frame: with Eppy's call it is her sign and her number in two voices, and it is an understatement about the pile.
The button: the voice says it fits, from behind the thing that does not.
screen: Larry asks; a letter zeta comes down behind the desk.

Amber's puppet says her call with its card up. As she says the handle, a follow spot finds an empty card stand at Sibyl's podium and an account plate for Zeta Of 1 lights in it. Her call card is marked REPLY and names no account it replied to.
zetaof1's reply card rises into the spot. Sibyl reads all of it. zetaof1 has no puppet.
Her proof card comes up, shrinks to the left edge and stays. Credit under it; glance label ZETA AT 1 · NOT THE HYPOTHESIS.

An upright bar lands for each term as she says it, in her brackets; the stage door opens on a queue of wider brackets. A count under each group, a guide line at half the last bar of the group before, and, as she finishes that sentence, the next clause of her post as a tag on the brackets, exactly as posted and marked at both ends. On her next line each group stacks into a slab marked with her sign.

Slabs drop on a pile by the desk, one per call from the sports desk. The brackets under her dots arrive twice as wide each time: the desk, the stage door, the wall. The pile covers Larry and leaves the frame; the crane follows and stops as she says her last line.
Her square lights on her card. dlowd's puppet says his reply with its card up. Wide shot, no host, Larry's voice from behind the pile.

length.estimate: The last fitted render was 88.9 seconds, with zetaof1's post whole, her step spoken and Eppy's longer calls. From there: his calls are short again, her call and her last line are whole again, and two waits are gone. About the same, a second or two less.
length.room: Nothing is cut for time, and nothing is cut or reworded for the voice.

forTheReviewer: One post beyond the two ideas' lists: her call to zetaof1 (3n2r4vvxhok24), which the terms list as usable and voiced. The terms make zetaof1's post usable 'as zetaof1's reply to shimmermathlabs' call', so the call is staged as the thing it replied to. Its own occasion was a question about what a zeta function is; Larry asks that in his own words (formats, 'ask what was asked'). The account that asked is not shown, read or named, and is not in this segment; its post is in sources.json only as the recorded context of her line. Her call card is marked REPLY and carries no reply-to handle.

zetaof1's post is read whole, with no cut. The last clause earns its place: it is zetaof1's own account of the handle, the wittiest thing in the post, and it puts 'I am large. I contain multitudes.' immediately before her line about a proof that fits, which is the turn of the segment. No house line picks the quotation up or repeats it.

Her proof is said in five lines, in order. One clause is cut from the voice, marked on the lines either side, and shown instead at the cue tag-k as a tag on the brackets, exactly as posted and marked at both ends: … more simply: block k has 2ᵏ terms, each ≥ 1/2ᵏ⁺¹, … The five spoken lines and the tag, put together, are her whole post, character for character; nothing of hers is left out or trimmed without a mark.

The tag at tag-k is unspoken text and longer than a glance, and it is left that way on purpose. It has no hold of its own: it goes up while her puppet is finishing the sentence it restates in symbols, stays on the brackets through her next line, and comes down when the first slab drops; the same clause lights on her card. Nobody has to read it to follow. If it is one unspoken thing too many, the choice is a sixth line for her puppet, not a trim.

The house speaks once inside her post, between 'so every block adds ≥ ½.' and 'infinitely many halves → ∞.': Eppy calls the slabs and Sibyl says 'At least.' Nobody asks her anything there, and her last line follows as the end of her post. 'At least' is her own phrase and her own sign; Eppy's call is the last word of the line she has just said, read off the slab.
Eppy's eight, sixteen and thirty-two are the next brackets under her dots by her own rule (twice as many terms as the last; 2ᵏ). They are not figures about anyone, and no step is added to her proof.
No house line, label or prop mentions the news, the hypothesis' proof or its size. The only label that names the hypothesis says this is not it. The button is set against the pile and nothing else.
House lines use no pronoun for a real person. Checked on 21 November 2026: none of the three accounts is on the opt-out list.

For whoever watches with sound (the owner's ruling of 21 November 2026: best effort on pronunciation is sufficient, as subtitles carry the line). Every change that had been made only for the voice is undone, so these are known to be said imperfectly, and each is carried by the caption and the card lighting the exact word as it is said: Eppy's one-word call; the half, and the word before the sign, in her step; the first words of her last line; the handle in her call; and the poet's name in zetaof1's last clause. The last is the one to look at. By ear the name has come out as other words, which can make the quotation sound like zetaof1's own statement; on screen the name and the quotation marks are lit at that moment on the card and in the caption. If, watching, that moment still reads as zetaof1 saying it of themselves, the remedy is a marked cut after 'infinity', which was fitted and heard correctly.
forTheSoundEditor: Restored to what was first written, for a best-effort pass: eppy-half-1 to eppy-half-6, amber-adds (a spoken line again), amber-infinity (whole), amber-call (with the handle) and sibyl-zeta (whole).

On each restored line I put back your own last respelling for that exact text where there was one ('Eight, terms', 'Sik-steen', the step, her last line, the handle, the last clause of zetaof1's post), and kept your current respelling for every word that was already there. Change any of it freely. No other line's text, `as`, rate or gap was touched.
amber-infinity: her closing square is not said. It lights on her card at the cue 'square'. The last token of the `as` is a silent stand-in so the word counts match.
The cue tag-k falls 0.9 seconds before the end of amber-brackets, so the tag goes up over the end of the sentence it restates. The waits after tag-k, after press and before amber-infinity are gone.
Eppy's six calls want a slab landing with each one; the gaps are a guess.
